newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian bank shares soar on improved results.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian bank shares soar on improved results.

text.p: Shares of Nigerias big banks rose on Wednesday on improved profit reports, traders said.
The all-share index closed at 7334.11 from 7314.10 on Tuesday.
Following on the trail of Union Bank which reported hefty rise in 1996 after-tax profit on Tuesday, FSB International Bank on Wednesday posted an equally impressive performance for 1996.

Traders reacted positively by pricing its shares 40 kobo higher at 7.50 naira. Traders, in hot pursuit of Union Bank shares, also raised its stocks by 22 kobo to 9.42 naira while First Bank and UBA were 10.40 naira and 8.15 naira, respectively 25 kobo and 10 kobo up.
But the continued offloading of PZ Industries shares further depressed the stock of the conglomerate which fell 30 kobo to 27.50 naira after losing 50 kobo on Tuesday.
Another big loser was Smithkline Beecham shares which closed 40 kobo lower at 8.04 naira after the exchange lifted a lid on its price since it concluded a merger with Sterling Products.

"The drop was because many investors wanted to sell the excess shares realised from a generous capitalisation just before the merger," said a dealer. "The shares will stabilise when the company releases its result."
Most other shares rose in a fairly active market, dealers said.
They included conglomerate UAC which rose 10 kobo to 9.50 naira and Lever Brothers, up five kobo to 17.30 naira.
Petroleum stocks closed stronger as demand firmed. African Petroleum finished at 52.20 naira, Mobil at 56.90 naira and National Oil at 53.80 naira, all 20 kobo up.
Persistent demand for food companies saw Cadbury and Nestle close 30 kobo more at 25.70 naira and 57.80 naira, respectively.
Vitafoam went ex-dividend at 3.76 naira, 35 kobo down.
